pharm: Highly selective HER2 tyrosine kinase inhibitor with minimal EGFR inhibition; penetrates the blood-brain barrier with activity against brain metastases
quick: 300 mg orally twice daily with trastuzumab + capecitabine
Can cause fetal harm; verify status; effective contraception during and after treatment per labeling
Do not breastfeed during treatment and after last dose per labeling
See full labeling; monitor renal function with diarrhoea/vomiting/dehydration risk
See full labeling; dose-reduce in moderate-severe impairment for hepatically cleared agents

CBC, LFTs, drug-specific toxicities, pregnancy status
summary: Tucatinib (Tukysa) with trastuzumab and capecitabine is indicated for HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer, including patients with brain metastases, after prior anti-HER2 therapy. HER2 selectivity spares EGFR, reducing skin toxicity versus older TKIs, but diarrhoea and hepatotoxicity require monitoring. Active in stable and active brain metastases (HER2CLIMB).
indications: HER2-positive unresectable or metastatic breast cancer, including brain metastases, in combination with trastuzumab and capecitabine, after at least one prior anti-HER2 regimen in the metastatic setting

dosage.d: 300 mg twice daily continuously, with trastuzumab (standard) and capecitabine 1000 mg/m2 twice daily days 1-14 of each 21-day cycle
dosage.t: Take at the same times daily, with or without food; swallow whole
dosage.n: Reduce to 200 mg BID in severe hepatic impairment; hold/reduce for grade 3+ diarrhoea or hepatotoxicity

admin: Take exactly as prescribed; do not crush, split or chew unless labeling allows
Take at the same time(s) each day; if a dose is missed follow the missed-dose rule - do not double
Report interacting new medicines including antifungals, anti-TB drugs, antiepileptics and St John's wort (CYP3A4)
Store in the original container with desiccant where supplied; protect from moisture
moa: Tucatinib is a potent HER2-selective tyrosine kinase inhibitor that blocks HER2 signalling with minimal EGFR inhibition. It crosses the blood-brain barrier, giving activity against CNS metastases when combined with trastuzumab and capecitabine.
preg: No adequate human data. Based on mechanism, fetal harm is expected. Verify pregnancy status before starting; advise effective contraception during treatment and for the specified period after the last dose. Use in pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential fetal risk.
lact: No data on presence in human milk. Because of potential serious adverse reactions in the breastfed infant, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for the specified period after the last dose.
renal: Mild-moderate impairment: no routine change unless labeled; severe: limited data - monitor for exaggerated toxicity and dehydration-related AKI.
hepatic: Mild impairment: monitor; moderate-severe: dose-reduce or avoid per labeling (most agents hepatically cleared).

major: Strong CYP3A4 inducers (reduce tucatinib exposure - avoid)
moderate: P-gp substrates including digoxin (tucatinib raises digoxin - monitor levels)
CYP3A4 substrates with narrow index (tucatinib inhibits CYP3A4)
interactions.alcohol: Avoid excess alcohol with hepatotoxic therapy.
interactions.diagnostics: No characteristic laboratory test interference; monitor disease-specific markers.

emergency: Severe diarrhoea with dizziness or reduced urine (dehydration) - seek urgent care
Yellowing of eyes/skin, dark urine (liver injury) - seek urgent evaluation

monitoring: LFTs (ALT/AST/bilirubin) every 3 weeks for 3 months then monthly
counsel: Diarrhoea is very common - keep antidiarrhoeal medicine ready and call early if watery stools persist
Report yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine or right-sided abdominal pain
Hand-foot redness/peeling comes mainly from capecitabine - moisturise and report blistering
Tell the team about new seizure, antifungal or TB medicines (interactions)
pk: Target inhibition within hours-days; response assessed in weeks
Room temperature 20-25 C in original container; protect from moisture
pearls: HER2CLIMB included active brain metastases with CNS progression benefit
EGFR-sparing design means less acneiform rash than lapatinib/neratinib, but diarrhoea remains prominent
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered on the same day unless it is near the next dose; never double up. Take as soon as remembered unless the next dose is due within 6 hours.
overdose: No specific antidote. Withhold drug and give supportive care with monitoring of CBC, ECG, LFTs and agent-specific toxicities. Contact Poison Help (1-800-222-1222).
